clue.text: Antoine, developing student at college

indicators.note: something developing is changing its form, so the letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young Frenchman called Antoine is maturing while studying at college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' rearranges the letters of ANTOINE. The college is Eton, the famous English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil of Eton College, the English public school, is called by this name.

clue.text: Perhaps Nero's representative during Rome uprising

indicators.note: uprising in a down clue means the whole is read from bottom to top
during means the short word sits within the city name

parts.note: taken as written
rep is short for representative, as in a sales rep

explanation.surface: Nero's agent at work during a rebellion in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' makes the container and 'uprising' turns the whole result, giving ROREPME read upwards. 'Perhaps' marks Nero as just one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero was a Roman ruler, one example of an imperial monarch.

clue.text: Widespread disgust shown by platform firing leader

indicators.note: firing means dismissing, so the leading letter of the platform word is sacked

parts.note: a podium is a raised platform for a speaker

explanation.surface: Public anger expressed from a stage after a party boss is sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firing leader' removes P, the first letter of PODIUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is general hatred or contempt felt by many people.

clue.text: Playwright's single book: 'Every Way But West'

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single
the compass points other than W are S, E and N

explanation.surface: A dramatist publishes one book with a quirky travel title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Every Way But West' looks like a title; it gives the remaining compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian dramatist who wrote A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler.

clue.text: Granny eager to find buff-coloured cloth

parts.note: nan is an informal word for grandmother
keen means eager

explanation.surface: A grandmother keen to find some pale yellowish fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth, originally from Nanjing, giving its name to the colour.

clue.text: Takes long steps in street, then trips

parts.note: rides are trips or journeys, as on a bus or horse

explanation.surface: Someone walks briskly along a street and then stumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trips' suggests stumbling, but here it means outings: rides.
explanation.definitionFit: Long purposeful steps are strides; the verb form matches 'takes long steps'.

clue.text: Sheer, the Parisian tower

parts.note: sheer means steep, as in a sheer cliff
le is French for the

explanation.surface: The sheer face of a Paris tower such as the Eiffel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Parisian' asks for French 'the', LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is a church tower topped by a spire.

clue.text: Ice, mostly, round edges of inner lake

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: ice can mean reserve, a cool aloofness of manner
O is round in shape

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Ice has mostly formed around the margins of an inland lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims RESERVE to RESERV; 'Ice' means coldness of manner, not frozen water.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservoir is an artificial lake used to store water.

clue.text: Idly draw wire in bomb

parts.note: to doodle is to draw idly
to wire a room is to bug it with a hidden microphone

explanation.surface: Someone sketches absent-mindedly while a bomb is wired up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wire' means plant a listening device, not connect a detonator.
explanation.definitionFit: Doodlebug was the British nickname for the German V-1 flying bomb in the Second World War.

clue.text: Dog someday must be trained

indicators.note: training shapes something anew, so the letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A puppy will have to be trained one day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be trained' rearranges SOMEDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Samoyed is a fluffy white Siberian breed of working dog.

clue.text: Rough seas in cup competition with jumps

indicators.note: rough water is churned up, so the letters of the following words are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailing cup race held in stormy seas, perhaps with boats leaping the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough' shuffles all of SEAS, IN and CUP together.
explanation.definitionFit: A puissance is a showjumping event in which horses tackle a few very high fences, including the famous wall.

clue.text: Wife returned, about to fly off the handle

indicators.note: about means the reversed title goes around the word to
returned means the title is read backwards

parts.note: MRS is the title of a married woman, so it stands for wife
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wife has come home and is on the point of losing her temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' gives SRM, which 'about' wraps around the next word; 'about to' reads as 'on the verge of' in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm is to rage angrily, the same as losing one's temper.

clue.text: An introduction to Chaucer in capital tale

indicators.note: in means the preceding letters sit inside the city

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
taken as written

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A literary introduction to Chaucer's tales delivered in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduction to' takes just the opening letter of Chaucer, and 'in' places that pair inside the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a story, especially a medieval tale of chivalry like those Chaucer told.

clue.text: Discussion involving singular herb

indicators.note: involving means the talk takes in the letter

parts.note: a parley is a discussion, especially between enemies
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A conversation about one particular herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' places S inside PARLEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsley is a common green culinary herb.

clue.text: Anagram in bottom row

definitions.note: used here as a verb: to anagram letters

parts.note: the rear is one's bottom or backside
a range is a row or line, as of mountains or cupboards

explanation.surface: A word puzzle printed in the bottom row of a grid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anagram' looks like an instruction to shuffle, but it is the definition, used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To make an anagram of a word is to put its letters in a different order.

clue.text: A tower erected to store produce in citadel

indicators.note: to store means to hold, so the crop goes inside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: erected in a down clue means built upwards, so the tower is read bottom to top

parts.note: a silo is a tall tower for storing grain
a crop is farm produce

explanation.surface: A grain tower built to hold farm produce within a fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tower ... to store produce' tempts as one definition of a silo; actually 'erected' reverses the tower and 'to store' wraps it with A around the produce.
explanation.definitionFit: An acropolis is the fortified upper citadel of an ancient Greek city, such as Athens.

clue.text: Cue employing a rest

indicators.note: employing means taking on, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a cue is a prompt or reminder
taken as written

explanation.surface: A snooker cue used with a rest to reach a shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cue' and 'rest' suggest snooker, where a rest supports the cue.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder is what is left over, the rest.

clue.text: Having a spherical shape bored out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Something round has been drilled hollow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges BORED.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbed means formed into an orb, a globe or ball.

clue.text: Drink needed after Foreign Office meeting

indicators.note: needed after places the drink behind the department's letters

parts.note: FO is the abbreviation for the UK Foreign Office
rum is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: Diplomats need a stiff drink after a Foreign Office meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed after' sets the order; the Foreign Office is Britain's ministry for overseas affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum is a gathering for open discussion, a type of meeting.

clue.text: Female I found wearing such a plastic flower

indicators.note: plastic means pliable and reshaped, so the letters are remoulded

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman wears an artificial plastic flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts I into SUCH A, and 'plastic' rearranges the lot to UCHSIA after F.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuchsia is a shrub with drooping pink and purple flowers.

clue.text: Pure blue appropriate

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling down
right means suitable or appropriate

explanation.surface: A shade of unmixed blue that is just right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' is the mood, not the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean utter or absolute, as in 'pure nonsense' or 'downright nonsense'.

clue.text: Lecturer bringing in about a million? You wish!

indicators.note: bringing in means the lecturer contains the letters

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer
re means about, concerning
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lecturer hopes to earn about a million but is told to dream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing in' makes the lecturer a container; 'about' is a piece meaning concerning, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Dream on!' is a scornful retort meaning the hope is unrealistic, just like 'You wish!'

clue.text: Animals (two of them) making heavy metal

parts.note: a wolf is one animal
the second of the two animals is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A pair of animals turned into a heavy metal band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavy metal' suggests rock music but means a dense element.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfram is another name for tungsten, a very dense metallic element.

clue.text: Climber to catch up on correct procedure detailed

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to net a fish is to catch it

indicators.note: detailed means de-tailed, the tail letter cut off

parts.note: the drill is the correct procedure for doing something

explanation.surface: A mountaineer must bring the correct climbing procedure up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NET into TEN; 'detailed' reads as de-tailed, removing the last L of DRILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is a slender shoot a climbing plant uses to cling to supports.

clue.text: Fancy better cereal

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it
rice is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: Someone would like a nicer breakfast cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like a verb or adjective but is a noun, a whim; 'better' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A caprice is a sudden whim, a passing fancy.

clue.text: I suffer, having backed lad's affair

indicators.note: backed means the words before it are read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
to ail is to suffer or be unwell
a son is a lad, a boy

explanation.surface: A rueful backer of a boy's romantic affair regrets it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having backed' gives LIAI; the 's after lad is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a secret love affair.

clue.text: One's job is delivering someone else's work

definitions.text: One's job is delivering someone else's work

parts.words: One's job is delivering someone else's work
parts.note: sounds like a courier, but the work delivered is a playwright's lines spoken on stage

explanation.surface: A courier or postman whose job is delivering other people's parcels.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage performer delivers the lines written by a dramatist, so it is literally another person's work.

clue.text: Plant's small advantage

parts.note: an edge is an advantage over a rival

explanation.surface: A factory has a slight competitive advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a factory but is a growing thing; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedge is a grass-like plant that grows in wet ground.

clue.text: Therefore cover is reliable

parts.note: so means therefore
a lid covers a pot or box

explanation.surface: An argument that a cover is dependable.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid means sound and dependable, as in 'a solid friend'.

clue.text: Queen in ruin or holding tax over

indicators.note: holding means the reversed tax sits between the two pieces

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin
taken as written

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the tax word is reversed

parts.note: a duty is a tax on goods

explanation.surface: A queen facing ruin or crushed by taxation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' gives YTUD, which 'holding' places in the middle of the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Tudor reigned as Mary I of England from 1553 to 1558.

clue.text: A loser staggering, out of energy, an unplaced competitor

indicators.note: staggering suggests reeling unsteadily, so the remaining letters lurch into a new order
out of means the letter goes missing from the words

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exhausted loser staggers home after failing to place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' leaves ALOSR, which 'staggering' turns into ALSOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Also-ran is racing slang for a horse, and so anyone, that finishes out of the places.

clue.text: Wonder about Lake poet

parts.note: a marvel is a wonder
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Musing on one of the Lake Poets such as Wordsworth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lake poet' suggests Wordsworth or Coleridge, but Lake is just L and the poet is Andrew Marvell; 'about' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew Marvell was a 17th-century English metaphysical poet, author of 'To His Coy Mistress'.
